subject: Zendo discovery: token profile, budget bands & SLO tradeoffs
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Chen <nora@zendo.ai>, Zendo Procurement <procurement@zendo.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Zendo discovery: token profile, budget bands & SLO tradeoffs

Hi Nora / procurement team —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone is aligned and we can map to concrete next steps. I’ve attached a short mutual action plan and a pricing snapshot for the bands we discussed.

Call highlights (short):
- Product flows: chat assist (user-facing, strict SLO), report-generation (background, tolerant).
- Estimated token volumes (monthly, ballpark): 100–250M tokens (mix of input+output).
- Peak user-facing QPS: ~25–40 concurrent user sessions (bursty evenings).
- Target procurement budget band mentioned on call: pref $7k–$15k/month but you asked for a target $/1M tokens to evaluate.
- Latency expectation: for the chat assist feature you indicated ~200–300ms P95 is ideal; report generation can tolerate 400ms+.

Cost / SLO trade-off overview (very high level):
- Option A — Hosted (fast onboarding): lowest engineering lift; for tight 200ms P95 we recommend streaming + smaller batching and higher-cost tier. Expected unit economics: ~$45–$60 per 1M tokens at 200ms P95 for the model family we demoed.
- Option B — Dedicated (reserved capacity): predictable throughput and better unit cost at scale. With moderate batching (batch sizes 8–16) and prefix/KV cache, we can land closer to ~$35–$50 per 1M tokens depending on committed monthly tokens and quantization profile. This is our recommended path if you want steady cost predictability.
- Option C — Private/VPC: for strict data residency; cost similar to Dedicated but with infra ops overhead.

Operational knobs we’ll use to tune latency vs cost:
- Streaming vs batch: streaming reduces tail latency for real-time flows (user-facing), batching reduces unit cost for background work.
- Batch size and max latency budget: increasing batch size improves tokens/second but raises tail latency.
- Quantization & model variant: 8-bit/4-bit quantization and smaller model variants reduce $/1M but can affect quality.

Immediate ask from you:
1) Confirm preferred monthly budget band (approx) you want us to target for quoting (A: <$7k, B: $7k–$15k, C: $15k+).
2) Confirm whether 200–300ms P95 is a hard SLO for chat assist, or whether 300–400ms would be acceptable to hit a lower unit price.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll loop in Rishi + Marcus to draft 2 quote scenarios (Conservative: meet 200ms P95; Lean: 350–400ms P95 and 20–30% lower unit cost).
- If budget aligns, run a short 2-week POC using a small dedicated pool to validate latency and actual $/1M tokens.

Attached: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_Zendo-v1.xlsx, redwood_pricing_band_snapshot.pdf

Can you confirm the budget band and SLO preference by end of week? Happy to set a 30-min follow-up.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

From: Nora Chen <nora@zendo.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Zendo Procurement <procurement@zendo.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Zendo discovery: token profile, budget bands & SLO tradeoffs

Thanks, Olga — really helpful summary and the attachments look good. A few clarifications from our side after the internal sync: 

- Monthly tokens: our initial projection is 120M–220M tokens/month in phase 1 (mix ~60/40 input/output). We can scale beyond that in Q3 next year.
- Budget band: procurement wants us to target the middle band initially (B: $7k–$15k/mo). Realistically, they’re comfortable with $9k–$12k/mo if the 200–300ms P95 for chat can be demonstrated.
- Target $/1M: procurement asked us to give a target $/1M they can evaluate vs other offers — around $45/1M tokens would make this easier to approve.
- SLO nuance: for the customer-facing chat assist we’d like to aim for <=300ms P95. If you can show a performance plan that lands 250–300ms P95 in a quick POC, procurement is happy to move forward. Background jobs can be 400–600ms.

Procurement also raised two quick questions:
1) Do you have a short SLA note for the dedicated tier (uptime, response for incidents)?
2) What are the terms for committed vs overage billing for reserved capacity?

Would be great to get your recommended two scenarios and a proposed POC cadence. Thanks — Nora
Nora Chen
Head of Product, Zendo.ai
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:10:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Zendo discovery: token profile, budget bands & SLO tradeoffs — internal ask

Team — forwarding Nora's clarifications. Quick internal summary / recommendation for quote and POC: 

Context: Nora confirmed 120–220M tokens/month and procurement prefers $9k–$12k/mo target if we can hit <=300ms P95 for chat. Their explicit target $/1M is ~ $45.

Our recommended approach (two scenarios):
- Scenario 1 (Conservative P95 250ms): Dedicated Standard pool, streaming for chat assist, small batch windows for background, reserved capacity commit for 3 months at a moderate discount. Estimated unit economics: ~$45–$52 per 1M tokens at 200–250ms P95. Estimated monthly cost (using 180M tokens midpoint): $8.1k–$9.4k. Upside: procurement-friendly latency and predictable billing.

- Scenario 2 (Cost-lean P95 350ms): Dedicated with larger batching for background, aggressive KV/prefix caching, quantized weights for some model variants. Estimated unit economics: ~$32–$38 per 1M tokens at 350ms P95. Estimated monthly cost (180M tokens): $5.8k–$6.8k. Risk: chat user experience may show slight increases in perceived latency unless we use streaming selectively.

Recommendations on configuration:
- Use streaming for all user-facing chat calls; set per-request streaming threshold so background tasks use batch path.
- Batch sizing: initial config batch target 8 for mixed workloads; allow temporary spikes with burst pools.
- POC plan: 2 weeks, mirror production traces (we should replay a subset of their traffic). Collect P95 and cost per 1M tokens at daily granularity.

Action items for quote
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Chen <nora@zendo.ai>, Zendo Procurement <procurement@zendo.ai>

Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Zendo discovery: token profile, budget bands & SLO tradeoffs

Nora — thanks for the quick responses and the clarity on budget. Per your ask we’ll produce two formal quote scenarios (Conservative P95 250ms and Cost-lean 350ms) and a 2-week POC plan.

Quick checklist / next steps: 
- I’ll upload the mutual action plan to the HubSpot deal and update with target dates: proposed POC kickoff Tue 2026-12-08.
- Marcus will draft the technical POC runbook and profiling checklist.
- Rishi will prepare the quote PDF + line items for committed vs overage terms.
- Procurement questions (SLA & billing): short answers included in the MAP; Rishi will include SLA bullets in the quote.

Links: HubSpot deal — https://app.hubspot.com/deals/67890 (I’ll add the MAP); MAP preview — https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-MAP-preview

If procurement can confirm the $9k–$12k/month target band and give us a list of any required PO/legal terms ahead of the POC, we’ll aim to have a signed MOU immediately following a successful POC.

Thanks everyone — will follow up with Marcus/Rishi’s artifacts by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Olga
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
